outcome: No lease was acquired; a successor claims immediately and completes the durable turn once.
The lost lease result expires; a successor polls, reclaims a higher generation, and completes once.
The lease is held but no run is admitted. The successor reclaims the lane and admits the unchanged durable ingress.
No admission has committed. The successor admits the run before selecting any input or executing an effect.
The admission committed but its response was lost. The successor resumes its durable identity and position before freezing the initial selection.
No orphaned input exists in the reference prefix; the successor reclaims the lease and executes its durable ingress once.
The admitted run has no frozen selection. The successor atomically selects its initial input and queued work.
The ordered selection and claims committed before the response was lost. The successor resumes those exact members with rotated physical claims.
No runtime progress was durable; the successor probes the same head and reclaims ingress.
The provider request is replayed from durable input with no committed model progress.
Partial provider stream state is process-local and discarded; the request is replayed.
The current lease remains valid but unrenewed; after expiry a successor reclaims it and executes the effect once.
The renewed lease result was lost; the renewed deadline eventually expires and a successor reclaims the turn without duplicating pre-effect work.
The group was not opened; the successor opens it and executes the child's external effect once.
The completed group-open result was lost before runtime progress; the receipt-less level-1 controller re-executes the external effect.
The tool attempt has not crossed the external boundary; recovery executes it once.
The external effect completed inside the tool but no durable outcome was recorded; recovery MUST re-execute it under at-least-once semantics.
The controller call returned but runtime progress was not durable; the receipt-less level-1 controller re-executes the external effect.
The settlement wait never ran; the child's effect already executed and the receipt-less level-1 recovery re-executes it.
The settlement read returned but its result was lost; the receipt-less level-1 recovery re-executes the child's external effect.
The group settled but was never closed; the receipt-less level-1 recovery re-executes the child's external effect.
The close result was lost; the receipt-less level-1 recovery re-executes the settled child's external effect.
Tool progress is not durable; active input and queued work remain reclaimable and the effect re-executes.
Checkpoint claims are pinned to the expired generation; the successor reclaims them and replays the uncommitted effect.
No tool outcome or model continuation is durable; the whole model-tool prefix is replayed.
Partial post-tool provider output is discarded. Level 1 replays the receipt-less effect; level 2 reuses the durable outcome before replaying the request.
The final checkpoint probe has not changed durable state; recovery replays the turn prefix.
Any final checkpoint claims remain generation-reclaimable; no model or effect outcome was committed.
The completion closure is not yet authorized; recovery replays the uncommitted turn prefix.
The exact completion closure is durably authorized; recovery settles it under the same store authority before redriving unfinished ingress.
The completion base gate is still open under the durable authorization; the successor settles the exact closure before replaying uncommitted ingress.
The completion base gate is sealed but input publication has not committed; recovery adopts the authorized winner and redrives the unfinished turn.
The final current-head CAS has not landed; recovery replays the checkpoint prefix and atomically settles its durable ingress claims with the recovered terminal turn.
The final CAS landed but its response was lost; the successor observes settled ingress and does not repeat the committed turn.
The final commit settled the admission and ingress. The successor returns its receipt without repeating the committed turn.

The final commit settled the admission and ingress; only the drain-end receipt is missing. The successor resumes the settled run and returns its receipt without executing another effect; this drain owns no children, so its replay has no end to write.

The drain-end receipt committed but its response was lost; the owner still holds the lane. After reclaiming it, the successor resumes the settled run and returns the terminal receipt without executing another effect.
The terminal receipt is durable but the owner still holds the lane. After reclaiming it, the successor returns the same receipt without executing another effect.
The lane release committed but its response was lost. The successor acquires the free lane and returns the durable terminal receipt.
A checkpoint executed before its outcome was finalized is reclaimed by the successor, which reaches the exact durable terminal state without stranding ingress.
After checkpoint authority is replaced and journaled by recovery, a second crash at final commit still recovers to the exact durable terminal state.

FIG-1573: with the crashed turn seeded without a next-turn row, recovery's drain claims no next-turn input and evaluates the orphan backstop while an active-turn row is still pinned to the very turn it is about to resume. The resumed turn keeps that row and delivers it at its own checkpoint, so recovery still reaches the exact durable terminal state with no ingress left behind; a sweep that took the row instead would change the replayed provider request.
After the peer releases its lease, durable admission reclaims its exact queued-work member under the recovery lease and settles it with the recovered terminal commit.

error_return.outcome: An unretried store error from execute_effect(ToolAttempt) aborts the turn as a controller error (FIG-3528): the typed error reaches the caller and no provider request or durable commit follows.

A session-retirement refusal (SessionDeleted, with its cause) from execute_effect(ToolAttempt) aborts the turn instead of recording a failed turn (FIG-3630): the retirement owns the turn, so no cancellation closure is authorized, no final head is committed, no provider request follows, and the typed refusal reaches the caller. Recording it would authorize a closure pin a deleted session can never settle, which then refuses the deletion.
An unretried store error from the effect journal's claim aborts the turn as a controller error (FIG-3528): the typed error reaches the caller and no provider request or durable commit follows.
An unretried store error from the effect journal's finalize aborts the turn as a controller error (FIG-3528): the typed error reaches the caller and no provider request or durable commit follows.

A store error from the effect-lease renew is a missed renewal, not a lost lease (FIG-3512, LeaseTimings' two-miss budget): the renewal loop retries it while the tool keeps running, the tool completes and finalizes, and the injected error never reaches the caller. This supersedes the FIG-3528 unretried-abort ruling for this placement: a single renew error is retried by design, so the fail-stop law's retried branch applies.
